license_note: The repository ships a LICENSE file carrying the verbatim Apache License 2.0 text, and the model card's own License section states that Apodex-1.1 is released under Apache 2.0. The grant covers the released weights and carries no revenue threshold, use restriction, or separate model-as-a-service licence, so the release is open source. The base checkpoint, Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, is itself Apache-2.0, so the fine-tune inherits a compatible grant. Apodex's own hosted service is governed separately by its Commercial Terms of Service, which is a service contract and does not qualify the weight licence.

license_evidence.scope: Official apodex/Apodex-1.1-mini repository: Safetensors weights, tokenizer, chat template, preprocessor and video-preprocessor configuration, and the official FP8, NVFP4, GPTQ-Int4, and GGUF exports and their derivatives
Pinned model card at the reviewed repository commit, whose License section states the release terms and whose YAML front matter declares license: apache-2.0 and the Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B base model

access_boundary: This record represents the apodex/Apodex-1.1-mini weight release published on Hugging Face at commit 4e4f109a5e32d1306dc6c75e4995a09c8b881811, the 35B-total, 3B-active multimodal mixture-of-experts checkpoint of the Apodex 1.1 generation. The unreleased full-size Apodex 1.1 model behind the Deep Discover tier, the Apodex 1.0 and 1.0-mini checkpoints and their 0.8B, 2B, and 4B SFT siblings, the official FP8, NVFP4, GPTQ-Int4, and GGUF format exports, the FrontierAgent and AgentCore harnesses, the Apodex Deep Research, Deep Solve, and Deep Discover product tiers, and OpenRouter's hosted route for the same weights are separate boundaries.
strengths: Ungated weights in an official Apodex Hugging Face organization, shipping the verbatim Apache-2.0 LICENSE file in the repository and stating the same terms in the card
Official FP8, NVFP4, GPTQ-Int4, and GGUF exports published by the developer on the same organization, so a consumer-GPU path needs no third-party repackaging

First-party model card publishes the recommended sampling parameters, the 262,144-token context and 32,768-token output budget, exact SGLang and vLLM launch commands with the Qwen3 tool-call and reasoning parsers, and a complete tool-using agent example

The FrontierAgent harness and the Apodex 1.1 technical report are published under the same organization, so the execution environment the model is trained for is inspectable rather than described only in prose
First-party documentation ties the 35B checkpoint to the Deep Research and Deep Solve platform tiers, and OpenRouter documents an independent hosted route
tradeoffs: Only the mini checkpoint is open; the full-size Apodex 1.1 model behind the Deep Discover tier is not published, so the generation's top capability is not obtainable as weights
The base is a Qwen3.5 checkpoint, so the release inherits that lineage's identity rather than standing as an independently pretrained model
The model card's benchmark results are reported for the Agent Team system configuration rather than for the bare checkpoint, so the published scores do not isolate the weights
No deprecation or versioning posture is published for the line, and release identity rests on repository commits with no dated snapshot names
